tools.name: start_site_audit
tools.description: Use this when the user asks for a technical SEO audit, a site crawl or an SEO health check of a website, or for broken links, redirect chains, duplicate or missing titles and meta descriptions, canonical, noindex or hreflang problems, sitemap errors, pages that are hard to find from the home page, o

tools.name: get_audit_status
tools.description: Use this after start_site_audit to check whether the audit has finished. Takes the audit_id. Returns status (queued, running, completed, failed or canceled), pages crawled so far, the page limit, and any notes or error text. If the status is failed, the error field says why (for example the site blo

tools.name: get_audit_report
tools.description: Use this once get_audit_status shows completed. Takes the audit_id and an optional top_n (1 to 25, default 10). Returns the issues ranked by likely impact, each with the number of affected pages, example URLs and a plain-English fix, plus a list of what was checked, what was not checked, and a note

tools.name: monitor_site
tools.description: Use this when the user wants Sitewalk to keep watching a website: check it regularly, re-audit it every day, week or month, or tell them when something breaks. Takes the site address and an optional frequency: daily, weekly or monthly (default monthly). Sitewalk audits the site again on that schedul

tools.name: list_monitored_sites
tools.description: Use this when the user asks which sites Sitewalk is monitoring, how often, or when the next check is. Returns each monitored site, its frequency, whether it is paused and the date of the next check. Needs a signed-in Sitewalk account.

tools.name: stop_monitoring
tools.description: Use this when the user wants Sitewalk to stop checking a site on a schedule. Takes the site address. Deletes that site's monitoring schedule; past audits and reports stay in the account. Needs a signed-in Sitewalk account.
